children: announced today it has completed its acquisition of Elisity, which is expected to improve IonQ's quantum security strategy by adding Zero Trust technology to its cyber capabilities.

"With the acquisition complete, IonQ now brings together post-quantum cryptography, quantum key distribution, and Zero Trust security in a single platform for the organizations that depend on it most," said IonQ CEO Niccolo de Masi.
IonQ shares were down 5% by late morning trading on Wednesday.

At closing, IonQ issued $1.15B of consideration in common stock under the terms of the merger agreement. The sellers may earn up to an additional $150M based on Elisity's performance against revenue milestones through January 2028. Elisity's current customers will continue to be supported by the same teams and platform.

"Our global customers depend on us to protect their networks every day," said Elisity CEO James Winebrenner. "Building on what we've learned across more than 100 deployments, we'll extend the Elisity platform customers already use to help them prepare for post-quantum cryptography."

On the same day, IonQ revealed a new partnership with QuantumCT, Connecticut's statewide initiative to accelerate quantum innovation and economic development in the state. The initiative is anchored by the University of Connecticut and Yale University, and it is supported by a coalition of industry, government and academic partners to position Connecticut as a national hub for quantum research, talent, and commercialization.

"Expanding access to advanced quantum computing resources is an important step in helping Connecticut's researchers, startups, and industry partners move from exploration to practical application," said QuantumCT interim CEO Vivek Ramakrishnan. "Our agreement with IonQ gives the QuantumCT ecosystem access to the trapped-ion platform, along with the technical support needed to put that capability to work."

title: IonQ completes Elisity acquisition and joins Conn. quantum initiative
